                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    # Three problem qubits: x0, x1, x2
    # Six ancillas: first one for phase, next five for clause results
    phase_ancilla = ancilla_qubits[0]
    clause_ancillas = ancilla_qubits[1:6]  # 5 ancillas

    # Clauses given in the problem
    clauses = [
        [(0, True),  (1, False), (2, True)],   # (x0 OR NOT x1 OR x2)
        [(0, False), (1, False), (2, True)],   # (NOT x0 OR NOT x1 OR x2)
        [(0, False), (1, False), (2, False)],  # (NOT x0 OR NOT x1 OR NOT x2)
        [(0, True),  (1, False), (2, False)],  # (x0 OR NOT x1 OR NOT x2)
        [(0, True),  (1, True),  (2, False)]   # (x0 OR x1 OR NOT x2)
    ]

    clause_info = []  # list of (control_qubits, inverted_qubits)

    # -------- Compute clause results ----------
    for i, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        anc = clause_ancillas[i]

        invert = []     # qubits that need an X before the mcx

            q = problem_qubits[q_idx]

                invert.append(q)   # positive literal -> check 0 -> need X

            qc.x(q)
        qc.mcx(controls, anc)
        for q in invert:
            qc.x(q)
        # Flip to clause satisfied: 1 iff clause is true

        # Restore the X gates (mirror of the restore step)
        for q in invert:
            qc.x(q)
        # mcx (self‑inverse) to clear the ancilla
        qc.mcx(controls, anc)
        # Undo the initial X gates (mirror of the prep step)
        for q in invert:

                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    # Unpack qubits for readability
    x = problem_qubits  # x[0] = x0, ..., x[3] = x3
    a = ancilla_qubits   # a[0..4] for clause results, a[5] for AND

    # Define each clause as a list of (index, is_positive)
    clauses = [
        [(0, False), (1, True), (3, False)],   # (~x0 ∨ x1 ∨ ~x3)
        [(0, False), (2, True), (3, True)],    # (~x0 ∨ x2 ∨ x3)
        [(0, True),  (1, False), (3, False)],  # (x0 ∨ ~x1 ∨ ~x3)
        [(0, True),  (1, True),  (2, True)],   # (x0 ∨ x1 ∨ x2)
        [(1, True),  (2, False), (3, False)]   # (x1 ∨ ~x2 ∨ ~x3)
    ]

    # ---- Compute each clause into a separate ancilla ----
    for i, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        anc = a[i]
        # Determine which problem qubits need an X before the Toffoli
        # (positive literals need X to check 0, negatives need no X)
        pos_indices = [idx for idx, is_pos in clause if is_pos]

            qc.x(x[idx])
        # Step B: 3-controlled X (flip ancilla if clause is FALSE)
        controls = [x[idx] for idx, _ in clause]  # all three after X-flips
        qc.mcx(controls, anc, mode='noancilla')
        # Step C: revert the flips
        for idx in pos_indices:
            qc.x(x[idx])
        # Step D: invert ancilla so it is |1> iff clause is TRUE
        qc.x(anc)

    qc.mcx(a[0:5], a[5], mode='noancilla')
    # Apply phase flip if all clauses satisfied

    # Uncompute AND (same operation, self‑inverse)

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],
                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    # Extract problem qubits
    x0 = problem_qubits[0]
    x1 = problem_qubits[1]
    x2 = problem_qubits[2]

    # Use three ancilla qubits for computation
    a0 = ancilla_qubits[0]   # will become (x0 OR NOT x2)
    a1 = ancilla_qubits[1]   # will become NOT x1
    a2 = ancilla_qubits[2]   # will become a0 AND a1 (the full predicate)

    # ---- Compute a0 = x0 OR NOT x2 ----
    # Using De Morgan: NOT( (NOT x0) AND x2 )
    qc.x(x0)                     # temporarily get NOT x0 on x0 line
    qc.ccx(x0, x2, a0)          # a0 = (NOT x0) AND x2
    qc.x(a0)                    # a0 = NOT( (NOT x0) AND x2 ) = x0 OR NOT x2
    qc.x(x0)                    # restore x0

    # ---- Compute a1 = NOT x1 ----
    qc.x(a1)                    # set a1 = 1 initially
    qc.cx(x1, a1)               # flip if x1=1 → a1 = 1 XOR x1 = NOT x1

    # ---- Compute a2 = a0 AND a1 (the predicate value) ----
    qc.ccx(a0, a1, a2)          # a2 = a0 & a1

    # ---- Apply phase flip: -1 iff a2 = 1 (i.e., f(x)=1) ----
    qc.z(a2)

    # ---- Uncompute everything in reverse order ----
    # Uncompute a2
    qc.ccx(a0, a1, a2)

    # Uncompute a1
    qc.cx(x1, a1)               # reverse of CX
    qc.x(a1)                    # reverse of initial X on a1

    # Uncompute a0 (exact reversal of its compute steps)
    qc.x(x0)                    # first step of reverse: flip x0 (as in compute)
    qc.x(a0)                    # flip a0 (as after CCX in compute)
    qc.ccx(x0, x2, a0)         # reverse of CCX
    qc.x(x0)                    # restore x0

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],
                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    """
    Implements a phase oracle for the 3‑SAT instance with 5 variables and 4 clauses.
    The oracle marks satisfying assignments with a phase of -1.
    """
    # Shorthand for qubits
    p = problem_qubits          # 5 qubits: x0..x4
    a = ancilla_qubits          # 5 ancillas: a[0..3] for clauses, a[4] scratch/final

    # ---------- Helper to compute a 3‑input AND into a target ancilla ----------
    def and3(bit0, bit1, bit2, target, scratch):
        """
        Compute target = bit0 AND bit1 AND bit2.
        scratch must be |0> initially and is returned to |0>.
        """
        # step 1: scratch = bit0 AND bit1
        qc.ccx(bit0, bit1, scratch)
        # step 2: target = scratch AND bit2
        qc.ccx(scratch, bit2, target)
        # uncompute scratch
        qc.ccx(bit0, bit1, scratch)


    # ---------- Compute each clause into a[0..3] ----------
    # Clause 0: (not x1 or not x2 or x3)   -> false when x1=1,x2=1,x3=0
    # Compute C0_false = x1 AND x2 AND (not x3) into a[0]
    qc.x(p[3])                          # flip x3 to get ¬x3
    and3(p[1], p[2], p[3], a[0], a[4])  # a[0] = C0_false
    qc.x(p[3])                          # restore x3
    qc.x(a[0])                          # invert to get clause true -> a[0] = C0_true

    # Clause 1: (not x0 or not x3 or not x4) -> false when x0=1,x3=1,x4=1
    # Compute C1_false = x0 AND x3 AND x4  (no negations needed)
    and3(p[0], p[3], p[4], a[1], a[4])  # a[1] = C1_false
    qc.x(a[1])                          # invert -> a[1] = C1_true

    # Clause 2: (x0 or x1 or x2) -> false when x0=0,x1=0,x2=0
    # Compute C2_false = (not x0) AND (not x1) AND (not x2)
    for q in [p[0], p[1], p[2]]:
        qc.x(q)                         # flip x0,x1,x2 to get ¬x0,¬x1,¬x2
    and3(p[0], p[1], p[2], a[2], a[4])  # a[2] = C2_false
    for q in [p[0], p[1], p[2]]:
        qc.x(q)                         # restore
    qc.x(a[2])                          # invert -> a[2] = C2_true

    # Clause 3: (not x1 or x2 or x4) -> false when x1=1,x2=0,x4=0
    # Compute C3_false = x1 AND (not x2) AND (not x4)
    for q in [p[2], p[4]]:
        qc.x(q)                         # flip x2,x4 to get ¬x2,¬x4
    and3(p[1], p[2], p[4], a[3], a[4])  # a[3] = C3_false
    for q in [p[2], p[4]]:
        qc.x(q)                         # restore
    qc.x(a[3])                          # invert -> a[3] = C3_true

    # ---------- Compute AND of all clause_true bits into a[4] ----------
    # a[4] = 1 iff all clauses are satisfied
    qc.mcx([a[0], a[1], a[2], a[3]], a[4], mode='noancilla')

    # ---------- Apply phase flip (Z) when clause accumulation = 1 ----------
    qc.z(a[4])

    # ---------- Uncompute the AND ----------
    qc.mcx([a[0], a[1], a[2], a[3]], a[4], mode='noancilla')

    # ---------- Uncompute each clause (reverse order) ----------
    # Clause 3
    qc.x(a[3])                          # restore a[3] to C3_false
    for q in [p[2], p[4]]:

    q = problem_qubits

    clause_anc = ancilla_qubits[:5]   # one per clause
    temp_anc = ancilla_qubits[5]      # used for decompositions

    #   - list of the three variable indices involved (in any order)

        ([0, 1, 2],   [0, 1, 2]),   # (x0 ∨ x1 ∨ x2)
        ([1],         [1, 2, 3])    # (x1 ∨ ¬x2 ∨ ¬x3)
    ]

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],
                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    """
    Phase oracle for the 3‑SAT instance:
      (¬x1 ∨ ¬x2 ∨ x3) ∧ (¬x0 ∨ ¬x3 ∨ ¬x4) ∧ (x0 ∨ x1 ∨ x2) ∧ (¬x1 ∨ x2 ∨ x4)
    """
    # Clause definitions: (variable_index, is_positive)
    #   True  -> literal = x_i
    #   False -> literal = ¬x_i
    clauses = [
        [(1, False), (2, False), (3, True)],   # ¬x1 ∨ ¬x2 ∨ x3
        [(0, False), (3, False), (4, False)],  # ¬x0 ∨ ¬x3 ∨ ¬x4
        [(0, True),  (1, True),  (2, True)],   # x0 ∨ x1 ∨ x2
        [(1, False), (2, True),  (4, True)],   # ¬x1 ∨ x2 ∨ x4
    ]

    # Ancilla allocation: first four for clause results, last for overall AND
    clause_anc = ancilla_qubits[:4]
    and_anc    = ancilla_qubits[4]

    # ---------- compute each clause ----------
    for i, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        controls = []
        flips = []                    # qubits to temporarily flip (positive literals)

        for var_idx, is_positive in clause:
            q = problem_qubits[var_idx]
            controls.append(q)
            if is_positive:
                flips.append(q)

        # Flip the positive literals so that the control acts on the complement
        for q in flips:
            qc.x(q)

        # Controlled-X: flip clause_anc iff all controls are 1
        qc.mcx(controls, clause_anc[i], mode='noancilla')

        # Restore flipped qubits
        for q in reversed(flips):
            qc.x(q)

        # Convert AND of complements into OR of literals
        qc.x(clause_anc[i])

    # ---------- overall AND of all clauses ----------
    qc.mcx(clause_anc[:4], and_anc, mode='noancilla')   # and_anc = (clause0 ∧ clause1 ∧ clause2 ∧ clause3)
    qc.z(and_anc)                                        # phase -1 iff and_anc = 1
    qc.mcx(clause_anc[:4], and_anc, mode='noancilla')   # uncompute

    # ---------- uncompute each clause (reverse order) ----------
    for i in reversed(range(4)):
        clause = clauses[i]
        controls = []
        flips = []

        for var_idx, is_positive in clause:
            q = problem_qubits[var_idx]
            controls.append(q)
            if is_positive:
                flips.append(q)

        # Uncompute step: reverse of compute
        qc.x(clause_anc[i])                              # undo last X on clause_anc
        for q in reversed(flips):                        # undo the second set of X gates
            qc.x(q)
        qc.mcx(controls, clause_anc[i], mode='noancilla') # undo mcx
        for q in flips:                                   # undo the first set of X gates
            qc.x(q)

    # All ancilla qubits are back to |0⟩

        ([2, 4, 5], [2, 4]),       # clause1: (x2 ∨ x4 ∨ ¬x5)
        ([1, 2, 4], [1, 2]),       # clause2: (x1 ∨ x2 ∨ ¬x4)
        ([1, 2, 5], [1, 2]),       # clause3: (x1 ∨ x2 ∨ ¬x5)
        ([0, 1, 4], []),           # clause4: (¬x0 ∨ ¬x1 ∨ ¬x4)
        ([0, 2, 4], [0, 2, 4]),    # clause5: (x0 ∨ x2 ∨ x4)
        ([0, 4, 5], [5])           # clause6: (¬x0 ∨ ¬x4 ∨ x5)
    ]

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],
                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    # Shortcuts for readability
    p = problem_qubits      # p[0]...p[4] correspond to x0...x4
    a = ancilla_qubits      # a[0]...a[4] are available ancillas

    # -------- Compute clause_false for each clause into a[0..3] ----------
    # Helper ancilla a[4] is used for the 3‑controlled NOT decompositions.

    # Clause 1: (¬x1 ∨ ¬x2 ∨ x3)
    # false iff x1=1, x2=1, x3=0
    qc.x(p[3])                                     # negate x3
    qc.ccx(p[1], p[2], a[4])
    qc.ccx(a[4], p[3], a[0])
    qc.ccx(p[1], p[2], a[4])
    qc.x(p[3])                                     # restore x3

    # Clause 2: (¬x0 ∨ ¬x3 ∨ ¬x4)
    # false iff x0=1, x3=1, x4=1
    qc.ccx(p[0], p[3], a[4])
    qc.ccx(a[4], p[4], a[1])
    qc.ccx(p[0], p[3], a[4])

    # Clause 3: (x0 ∨ x1 ∨ x2)
    # false iff x0=0, x1=0, x2=0
    qc.x(p[0]); qc.x(p[1]); qc.x(p[2])
    qc.ccx(p[0], p[1], a[4])
    qc.ccx(a[4], p[2], a[2])
    qc.ccx(p[0], p[1], a[4])
    qc.x(p[0]); qc.x(p[1]); qc.x(p[2])

    # Clause 4: (¬x1 ∨ x2 ∨ x4)
    # false iff x1=1, x2=0, x4=0
    qc.x(p[2]); qc.x(p[4])
    qc.ccx(p[1], p[2], a[4])
    qc.ccx(a[4], p[4], a[3])
    qc.ccx(p[1], p[2], a[4])
    qc.x(p[2]); qc.x(p[4])

    # a[0..3] now hold clause_false (1 if clause unsatisfied)

    # -------- Convert to clause_true and combine into overall AND ----------
    # Mark states where all clauses are true -> apply phase -1
    # First flip: clause_true = NOT clause_false
    for i in range(4):
        qc.x(a[i])

    # Compute overall AND of a[0..3] into (temporary) problem qubits p[0], p[1]
    # Use a[4] as first helper, then p[0], p[1] as helpers for the tree.
    qc.ccx(a[0], a[1], a[4])          # a[4] = a0 & a1
    qc.ccx(a[2], a[3], p[0])          # p[0] = a2 & a3
    qc.ccx(a[4], p[0], p[1])          # p[1] = (a0&a1) & (a2&a3) = overall AND

    # Phase gate on the result
    qc.z(p[1])

    # Uncompute the AND tree (reverse order)
    qc.ccx(a[4], p[0], p[1])
    qc.ccx(a[2], a[3], p[0])
    qc.ccx(a[0], a[1], a[4])

    # Restore clause_false (undo the flip)
    for i in range(4):
        qc.x(a[i])

    # a[0..3] now hold clause_false again, a[4] is 0, p[0],p[1] are back to original

    # -------- Uncompute clause_false (reverse of the compute steps) ----------

    (¬x0 ∨ ¬x2 ∨ x3) ∧ (x0 ∨ x1 ∨ x2) ∧ (x0 ∨ ¬x1 ∨ ¬x2) ∧
    (¬x0 ∨ x1 ∨ x2) ∧ (¬x0 ∨ x1 ∨ ¬x2) ∧ (x1 ∨ x2 ∨ x3)

    Qubits: problem_qubits[0..3] store x0..x3.
    Ancillas: ancilla_qubits[0..6] available.
    """
    # Helper function to compute a 3-literal clause into a target ancilla.
    # The clause is true iff at least one literal is true.
    # The circuit is self-inverse (its own inverse).
    def apply_clause(literals, target, scratch):
        # literals: list of (qubit, is_negated)
        # For each literal that is positive (not negated), we need to flip the qubit
        # before the AND of false conditions. We'll apply X, then later undo.
        for q, neg in literals:
            if not neg:   # positive literal -> false condition requires qubit=0
                qc.x(q)
        # The three qubits now represent: for each literal, the qubit is 1 iff the
        # literal is false (because of the X flips on positive literals).
        c1, c2, c3 = [q for q, _ in literals]
        # Compute AND of the three conditions into target, using scratch as temporary.
        qc.ccx(c1, c2, scratch)        # scratch = c1 & c2
        qc.ccx(scratch, c3, target)    # target ^= scratch & c3
        qc.ccx(c1, c2, scratch)        # uncompute scratch (back to 0)
        # Invert to get clause truth
        qc.x(target)
        # Restore X on positive literals
        for q, neg in reversed(literals):
            if not neg:
                qc.x(q)

    p = problem_qubits
    a = ancilla_qubits

    # Each clause as list of (qubit, is_negated)
    clauses = [
        [(p[0], True),  (p[2], True),  (p[3], False)],  # clause 1
        [(p[0], False), (p[1], False), (p[2], False)],  # clause 2
        [(p[0], False), (p[1], True),  (p[2], True)],   # clause 3
        [(p[0], True),  (p[1], False), (p[2], False)],  # clause 4
        [(p[0], True),  (p[1], False), (p[2], True)],   # clause 5
        [(p[1], False), (p[2], False), (p[3], False)]   # clause 6
    ]

    # Store clause truth into a[0]..a[5]
    # Use a[6] as scratch for Toffoli decompositions

    # We want to set a[6] = 1 iff all a[0..5] are 1.
    # Use the 4 problem qubits as scratch (they are restored to original state).

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],
                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    # Clauses as lists of (variable_index, is_positive)
    # is_positive True -> literal is x_i, False -> NOT x_i
    clauses = [
        [(3, True),  (4, False), (7, False)],   # (x3 OR NOT x4 OR NOT x7)
        [(2, True),  (4, True),  (7, False)],   # (x2 OR x4 OR NOT x7)
        [(2, True),  (3, True),  (6, True)],    # (x2 OR x3 OR x6)
        [(2, True),  (3, False), (6, True)],    # (x2 OR NOT x3 OR x6)
        [(1, False), (4, False), (5, True)],    # (NOT x1 OR NOT x4 OR x5)
        [(3, True),  (6, True),  (7, True)],    # (x3 OR x6 OR x7)
        [(0, False), (3, False), (4, False)]    # (NOT x0 OR NOT x3 OR NOT x4)
    ]

    # Helper to compute a single clause into a dedicated ancilla.
    # The clause ancilla is initially |0> and after the routine holds the OR of the three literals.
    # The helper ancilla (ancilla_qubits[7]) is used as temporary and returned to |0>.
    # Problem qubits are returned to their original states.
    def compute_clause(clause_idx: int, literals):
        # Allocate ancillas
        clause_anc = ancilla_qubits[clause_idx]
        helper = ancilla_qubits[7]

        # Flip problem qubits for positive literals (so we later compute AND of negated literals)
        for var, pos in literals:
            if pos:
                qc.x(problem_qubits[var])

        # Compute AND of the three (flipped) qubits into clause_anc using the 3‑controlled X trick
        ctrl = [problem_qubits[var] for var, _ in literals]
        qc.ccx(ctrl[0], ctrl[1], helper)          # helper = c1 & c2
        qc.ccx(ctrl[2], helper, clause_anc)       # clause_anc = (c1 & c2 & c3)
        qc.ccx(ctrl[0], ctrl[1], helper)          # restore helper to |0>

        # Invert to get OR: clause_anc now holds OR of the original literals
        qc.x(clause_anc)

        # Restore problem qubits
        for var, pos in reversed(literals):
            if pos:
                qc.x(problem_qubits[var])

    # Reverse helper: undoes the compute step
    def uncompute_clause(clause_idx: int, literals):
        clause_anc = ancilla_qubits[clause_idx]
        helper = ancilla_qubits[7]

        # First toggle back to AND of negations
        qc.x(clause_anc)

        # Flip problem qubits again (same as in compute)
        for var, pos in literals:
            if pos:
                qc.x(problem_qubits[var])

        # Uncompute the AND using the same three Toffolis
        ctrl = [problem_qubits[var] for var, _ in literals]
        qc.ccx(ctrl[0], ctrl[1], helper)
        qc.ccx(ctrl[2], helper, clause_anc)
        qc.ccx(ctrl[0], ctrl[1], helper)

        # Restore problem qubits
        for var, pos in reversed(literals):
            if pos:
                qc.x(problem_qubits[var])

    # ---------- Compute all clauses ----------
    for idx, lit in enumerate(clauses):
        compute_clause(idx, lit)

    # ---------- Global phase: -1 iff all clause ancillas are 1 ----------
    control_qubits = [ancilla_qubits[i] for i in range(7)]

    qc.mcx(control_qubits, target, mode='noancilla')

        [(2, False), (5, False), (6, False)],   # (x2 OR x5 OR x6)

    ancilla_qubits: 8 ancilla qubits (0..6 for clause flags, 7 for temporary)
    """

    # is_negated = True means the literal is ¬var, False means var itself.

        [(0, True),  (2, True),  (4, False)],   # ¬x0 ∨ ¬x2 ∨ x4
        [(2, False), (4, False), (5, True)],    # x2 ∨ x4 ∨ ¬x5
        [(1, False), (2, False), (4, True)],    # x1 ∨ x2 ∨ ¬x4
        [(1, False), (2, False), (5, True)],    # x1 ∨ x2 ∨ ¬x5
        [(0, True),  (1, True),  (4, True)],    # ¬x0 ∨ ¬x1 ∨ ¬x4
        [(0, False), (2, False), (4, False)],   # x0 ∨ x2 ∨ x4
        [(0, True),  (4, True),  (5, False)],   # ¬x0 ∨ ¬x4 ∨ x5
    ]

    a = ancilla_qubits          # alias
    temp = a[7]                 # shared temporary

    # Phase 1: Compute unsatisfied flags for each clause
    #   a[i] = 1 iff clause i is unsatisfied
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i, clause in enumerate(clauses):

        inverted_qubits = []

        # Prepare literals: X on problem qubits for positive literals.
        # After this, the value on the wire is 1 iff the literal is FALSE.

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],
                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    """
    Implements a Grover oracle for the 3-SAT problem:
      (x0 OR x4 OR NOT x5) AND
      (NOT x2 OR x4 OR NOT x5) AND
      (x0 OR x1 OR NOT x4) AND
      (NOT x1 OR x4 OR x5) AND
      (x0 OR NOT x2 OR NOT x3) AND
      (x1 OR x2 OR x3)
    using the compute-phase-uncompute discipline.
    """
    # List of clauses: each clause is a list of (variable, is_positive) tuples
    clauses = [
        [(0, True), (4, True), (5, False)],   # x0 OR x4 OR NOT x5
        [(2, False), (4, True), (5, False)],  # NOT x2 OR x4 OR NOT x5
        [(0, True), (1, True), (4, False)],   # x0 OR x1 OR NOT x4
        [(1, False), (4, True), (5, True)],   # NOT x1 OR x4 OR x5
        [(0, True), (2, False), (3, False)],  # x0 OR NOT x2 OR NOT x3
        [(1, True), (2, True), (3, True)]     # x1 OR x2 OR x3
    ]

    # Assign ancilla indices for convenience
    a = ancilla_qubits          # a[0]..a[5] for clause results, a[6] as scratch and for MCZ

    # Compute phase: store each clause result in a clause ancilla -----------------
    for i, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        # Apply X on problem qubits for positive literals
        for var, sign in clause:
            if sign:
                qc.x(problem_qubits[var])

        # Extract the three problem qubits involved in this clause
        # Use the order as given in the clause definition
        p0 = problem_qubits[clause[0][0]]
        p1 = problem_qubits[clause[1][0]]
        p2 = problem_qubits[clause[2][0]]

        # Compute (NOT L0 AND NOT L1) into scratch (ancilla[6])
        # Actually we compute (p0 AND p1) into a[6]
        qc.ccx(p0, p1, a[6])
        # Compute (scratch AND p2) into a[i] -> a[i] = p0 AND p1 AND p2
        qc.ccx(a[6], p2, a[i])
        # Invert a[i] to get clause satisfied (OR of literals)
        qc.x(a[i])
        # Uncompute the scratch qubit
        qc.ccx(p0, p1, a[6])

    # Using phase kickback: H, MCX, H on the scratch ancilla (now clean)
    qc.h(a[6])
    qc.mcx(a[0:6], a[6], mode='noancilla')

        p1 = problem_qubits[clause[1][0]]

    # The gate sequence sets t = a OR b, leaving a, b unchanged.
    # t is assumed to be |0> before the call.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def or_into(target: int, a: int, b: int) -> None:
        qc.x(target)                     # t = 1
        qc.x(a); qc.x(b)                # flip a,b
        qc.ccx(a, b, target)            # if both 0 (now 1), flip t
        qc.x(a); qc.x(b)                # restore a,b

    # Helper: AND of four qubits (q0..q3) into target (must be 0).
    # Uses two scratch ancillas (s1, s2) that are restored.

        qc.ccx(q0, q1, s1)              # s1 = q0 & q1
        qc.ccx(q2, q3, s2)              # s2 = q2 & q3
        qc.ccx(s1, s2, target)          # target = s1 & s2 = (q0&q1)&(q2&q3)

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],
                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    """
    Implements a Grover phase oracle for the vertex cover problem:
    f(x) = 1 iff x describes a vertex cover of size ≤ 2 for the graph
    with 6 vertices and edges:
        (0,3), (1,2), (2,3), (2,4), (2,5), (3,4).
    Only the state |0,0,1,1,0,0> (vertices 2 and 3 selected, others not)
    satisfies the predicate.

    # Apply X on problem qubits that must be 0 (indices 0,1,4,5)
    zero_qubits = [0, 1, 4, 5]
    for q in zero_qubits:
        qc.x(problem_qubits[q])

    # Now all problem qubits are |1⟩ for the target state.
    # Use a multi-controlled X (Toffoli with 6 controls) to flip ancilla[0]
    # when all 6 problem qubits are 1.
    # Provide ancilla_qubits[1:5] as workspace for the decomposition.
    qc.mcx(problem_qubits, ancilla_qubits[0],
           ancilla_qubits=ancilla_qubits[1:5], mode='ancilla')

    # Apply phase -1 on the state where ancilla[0] is |1⟩.
    qc.z(ancilla_qubits[0])

    # Uncompute the multi-controlled X.
    qc.mcx(problem_qubits, ancilla_qubits[0],
           ancilla_qubits=ancilla_qubits[1:5], mode='ancilla')

    # Restore the problem qubits to their original state.
    for q in zero_qubits:
        qc.x(problem_qubits[q])

    Marks the basis state |x> with phase -1 iff sum_{i} x_i * a_i == 24.

    # Compute carry (majority) into a4

    qc.cx(x3, a5)

    qc.cx(x3, a5)

    qc.cx(a5, a4)

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],
                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    """
    Grover phase oracle for the 3x3 Latin square completion problem.

    The grid (rows top to bottom, '.' = free cell):
      . . 1
      1 . 2
      2 . 0

    Free cells (row, col): (0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (2,1).
    Each free cell uses 2 problem qubits (low bit b0, high bit b1):
      code = b0 + 2*b1, decoded: 00->0, 01->1, 10->2, 11->0.

    The oracle marks with phase -1 exactly those assignments which
    yield a valid Latin square (every row and column contains 0,1,2 once).

    Uses 4 ancillas for sub‑conditions and 1 ancilla for the multi‑controlled Z.
    The sixth ancilla is unused.
    """
    # Assign ancillas
    a0 = ancilla_qubits[0]  # flag: cell (0,0) == 0
    a1 = ancilla_qubits[1]  # flag: cell (0,1) == 2
    a2 = ancilla_qubits[2]  # flag: cell (1,1) == 0
    a3 = ancilla_qubits[3]  # flag: cell (2,1) == 1
    target = ancilla_qubits[4]  # target for MCZ, prepared in |1>

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Compute flags
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # flag a0: cell (0,0) == 0  ↔  (q0 == q1)
    qc.cx(problem_qubits[0], a0)
    qc.cx(problem_qubits[1], a0)
    qc.x(a0)

    # flag a1: cell (0,1) == 2  ↔  (q2==0 and q3==1)
    qc.x(problem_qubits[2])
    qc.ccx(problem_qubits[2], problem_qubits[3], a1)
    qc.x(problem_qubits[2])

    # flag a2: cell (1,1) == 0  ↔  (q4 == q5)
    qc.cx(problem_qubits[4], a2)

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],
                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    """
    Implements a Grover phase oracle for a pattern matching problem.

    Given a binary text of length 8 and a pattern "1111" (no wildcards),
    the oracle applies a phase of -1 to exactly those computational basis
    states where the pattern appears as a contiguous substring at some
    offset o in 0..4.

    The oracle uses 6 ancilla qubits: 5 to store individual substring
    matches and 1 to compute their logical OR.
    """
    # Split ancilla qubits: 0..4 for substring ANDs, 5 for OR
    a_and = ancilla_qubits[0:5]   # one per possible offset
    a_or  = ancilla_qubits[5]     # final OR

    # Helper to compute AND of 4 consecutive text bits into an ancilla
    def compute_and_into(offset: int, target: int):
        controls = [problem_qubits[offset + i] for i in range(4)]
        qc.mcx(controls, target, None, mode='noancilla')

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Compute all 5 substring matches (ANDs)
    #    a_and[o] = s_o & s_{o+1} & s_{o+2} & s_{o+3}
    for o in range(5):
        compute_and_into(o, a_and[o])

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Compute OR of the 5 substring matches into a_or
    #    Using De Morgan: OR(a_i) = NOT(AND(NOT(a_i)))
    #    a) Invert all a_and
    for i in range(5):
        qc.x(a_and[i])

    #    b) Compute AND of inverted bits into a_or
    qc.mcx(a_and, a_or, None, mode='noancilla')

    #    c) Invert a_or to obtain OR
    qc.x(a_or)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Apply the phase flip if OR == 1 (i.e., set a_or to |1>)
    qc.z(a_or)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Uncompute the OR computation (mirror of step 2)
    qc.x(a_or)                     # undo inversion of a_or
    qc.mcx(a_and, a_or, None, mode='noancilla')  # undo AND
    for i in range(5):
        qc.x(a_and[i])             # undo inversion of a_and

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Uncompute the substring ANDs (mirror of step 1)
    for o in range(5):
        compute_and_into(o, a_and[o])
